title: Source problem
account: The open question was posed during the Simons Institute’s 2015 Economics and Computation program and documented in arXiv:2610.08796. It asks for an exact polynomial-time equilibrium algorithm in the explicitly described model.

title: Earlier working drafts
account: The collection supplies the rank-one and fixed-type algorithms, threshold ordering, rent-division embedding, and normalized approximation argument. Collins supplied it as a lead. The L3 review identifies overlap, checks the arguments and gives an endpoint correction.

title: Branching investigation and prior-work search
account: Asked for a persistent branching tree, early searches for prior partials, model-assisted investigation of individual questions, and a record of useful next directions.

title: Classify the longest single continuation run
account: Asked whether a restricted Busy Beaver quantity for each class of inputs could tighten the upper bound. Collins later explicitly confirmed this as his contribution to the manuscript. Codex developed the signature counts, bounds and examples. The later shortest-path reduction has separate attribution.

title: Track Hall certificates and the size of exact intermediate states
role: Follow-up questions recorded in L1 and L2
account: L1 proposed counting changes of maximizing Hall witnesses in a fixed phase. The handoff traced that suggestion through B3e, where the full family of maximizing sets changes at a fixed threshold. L1a now isolates strict threshold drops. L2 identified the input-only denominator question for its exact continuation.

title: Pursue the unresolved continuation case
account: Asked why the classification left a case unresolved and requested continued investigation at 03:11 UTC. The work compared reachable states with changes forced on one run, developed a fixed-flow counterexample, and recorded a separate proof audit.

title: Expose the scope of the counterexample
account: Commissioned a readable standalone sketch, specified his provisional human byline and motivation, and requested separate disclosure of both models. The parametric shortest-path theorem is due to Gajjar and Radhakrishnan. Sol reviewed literature and tested small instances. Astra helped develop and check the reduction and draft the text.

title: Open the first A4 market investigation and connect its findings to the graph
account: Asked what was missing from L3/A4 after the continuation lower bound. L3 had already identified the market oracle. The first A4 pass derived a candidate certificate and bounds for two directional auctions. At 04:03 UTC Collins asked that the results go back to the main investigation and that the graph have an editable source. The main investigation incorporated them by 04:07 UTC.

title: Check the library pieces for a constructive proof
account: Requested a paper-shaped constructive Lean development, beginning with a working environment and small library tests. The checked deliverable is the library-check package. A full formalization remains a separate task.

title: Switch from tracing the path to the market oracle
account: After the continuation obstruction, selected A4 for the next investigation. The market correspondence and oracle route had already been identified in earlier work. The research pass developed the structural solvers, clearing reduction and complementarity formulation.

title: Try fractional bipartite covering
account: Identified the resemblance to fractional vertex cover and asked whether an exact covering LP, reweighting, or Hall feedback could recover a clearing flow. The resulting notes derive descent, special cases and counterexamples for changing demand graphs.

title: Transfer market structure and examine the Newton bound
account: Requested a transfer from A4 back to L1/L2, supplied the sufficient-LCP preprint, and directed a parallel search for an equivalent low-handicap formulation. The reports give exact budget recovery and limitations of scaling, with conditional formulations.

title: Use maze search as an analogy for bounded support search
role: Proposed analogy in the research discussion
account: Asked whether maze solvers that relax optimality or completeness could inform A4d. The pass developed exact verification after bounded search, price lists from anchored paths, and lower bounds for particular search rules.

title: Require a short list that contains a solution
account: Asked for polynomially many candidates guaranteed to include an exact answer, building on the search finisher. The resulting work separates the number of region queries from the computational cost of choosing a useful query.

title: Audit the full-table count and exploit one supplied capacity
account: Directed an audit of the proposed all-capacity counting hardness argument and a study of capacity-specific pruning, including the toll-road analogy. The resulting work separates the hard aggregate count from positive results for one supplied instance.

title: Grow an alternating forest after a failed Hall test
account: Submitted the Hungarian-algorithm analogy as a first route. Asked about tight partial flows, exact next events and binary-time progress. The report obtains exact safe jumps and a fixed-deficit family with many events.

title: Certify and contract a forced price relation
account: Submitted the generalized-flow analogy as the second route. Asked whether a forced tie permits eliminating a price while preserving the two capacities. The report gives certificates, recovery and limits of discovering a specific tie.

title: Use dominance only when all completions survive
account: Requested this budgeted-shortest-path analogy after the first two routes if needed. The report obtains one representative at fixed boundary quotes and an antichain obstruction for lists of committed residual loads.

title: Use price jumps to find and test contractions
role: Proposed combination and supplied an example
account: Proposed feeding price-jump events into forced-tie tests, contracting certified relations, and using fixed-quote dominance after contraction. Supplied a three-buyer market where an ascent tie disappears before the minimum.

title: Use existing solvers to close gaps across the market and game approaches
role: Selected the research direction and supplied the comparison
account: Connected A4h9's jump and contraction loop to B3d's fixed-quote switching and L4b's fixed-threshold endpoints. Asked which existing results could solve missing steps in the other approaches.
